title: 2009 HMMT November General Round 2 Problem 3
statement: Let \(C\) be the circle of radius 12 centered at \((0,0)\). What is the length of the shortest path in the plane between \((8 \sqrt{3}, 0)\) and \((0,12 \sqrt{2})\) that does not pass through the interior of \(C\) ?

solutions.text: \(12+4 \sqrt{3}+\pi\) The shortest path consists of a tangent to the circle, a circular arc, and then another tangent. The first tangent, from \((8 \sqrt{3}, 0)\) to the circle, has length \(4 \sqrt{3}\), because it is a leg of a 30-60-90 right triangle. The \(15^{\circ}\) arc has length \(\frac{15}{360}(24 \pi)\), or \(\pi\), and the final tangent, to \((0,12 \sqrt{2})\), has length 12.
